c925b35cdf45.summary: An experimental pill prevented a measles-like virus from spreading through the air or through close contact in ferrets. Researchers say the drug could one day complement vaccination and make outbreaks easier to contain.

73907a0344fc.title: Ancient ape fossil in Egypt challenges the story of human origins
73907a0344fc.summary: A newly identified fossil ape from northern Egypt is reshaping ideas about where the ancestors of modern apes first emerged. Analyses place it closer to living apes than any known East African species of the same age, pointing to North Africa and the Middle East as a possible birthplace and crossroads for the ape lineage that eventually produced gibbons, orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, and humans.

1bc0a390f33d.summary: A large study suggests that GLP-1 drugs including Ozempic and Mounjaro may slightly increase the risk of hair loss in people with type 2 diabetes. 043a95ecdd71.summary: Обнаружен новый вид гигантской саламандры, *Limnospondylus ajimuensis*, на основе окаменелостей возрастом 3,5 миллиона лет, найденных в Японии. Этот вид, живший в более теплом и влажном климате Кюсю, мог достигать 1,1 метра в длину, что указывает на возможность существования еще неидентифицированных видов гигантских саламандр среди ранее классифицированных окаменелостей.
043a95ecdd71.original_description: Fossils discovered in Japan more than two decades ago have finally been identified as a new genus and species of giant salamander. Limnospondylus ajimuensis lived around 3.5 million years ago in a warmer, wetter Kyushu and may have reached 1.1 meters in length. Its discovery hints that many more unknown giant salamanders could be hiding among fossils previously given the wrong classification.

d1c7054cb2a3.title: Scientists discover the hidden brain switch that assigns bees their jobs
d1c7054cb2a3.summary: Researchers found that specific brain circuits help decide which jobs bees perform as they age. When those circuits were switched off, older worker bees began caring for the queen again instead of carrying out their normal later-life duties. The findings reveal that a bee colony’s complex division of labor may be guided by neural switches hidden inside each bee’s brain.
